function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Here are some great ways to order a cake, whether you’re looking for a local bakery, a national chain, or an online delivery service. Pick the option that best fits your needs (location, style, budget, etc.): | Option | What it offers | How to order | Tips | |--------|----------------|--------------|------| | **Local Artisan Bakeries** | Fresh, handmade cakes with unique flavors and designs. | • Search “cake shop near me” on Google Maps or Yelp.
• Call or visit the bakery’s website.
• Many accept online orders via their site or a simple email. | • Ask about custom designs and flavor combos.
• Book at least 1–2 weeks in advance for special occasions. | | **National Cake Delivery Chains** | Consistent quality, nationwide coverage, often with same‑day delivery. | • **Goldbelly** – delivers specialty cakes from famous bakeries across the U.S.
• **BakeShop** – offers a wide range of cakes, cupcakes, and pastries. | • Check delivery times and shipping fees.
• Look for “gift wrap” or “personalized message” options. | | **Grocery Store Chains** | Convenient, often free delivery with grocery pickup. | • **Walmart Grocery**, **Kroger**, **Safeway**, **Whole Foods** – all have online ordering and delivery. | • Use the “Bakery” section on the app or website.
• Some stores offer “same‑day” or “next‑day” delivery. | | **Online Specialty Cake Shops** | Custom cakes, themed designs, and premium ingredients. | • **CakeBoss** – custom cakes with a design tool.
• **Etsy** – find local bakers who ship nationwide.
• **The Cake Shop** – offers a variety of ready‑made and custom cakes. | • Read reviews and check delivery policies.
• For custom orders, provide clear instructions and photos. | | **Food Delivery Apps** | Quick, often same‑day delivery from local restaurants. | • **DoorDash**, **Uber Eats**, **Grubhub** – search “cake” or “bakery.” | • Delivery fees may apply; check for promotions.
• Some apps allow you to add a note for the baker. | | **Specialty Dessert Shops** | Gourmet desserts, often with a boutique feel. | • **Magnolia Bakery**, **Baked by Melissa**, **Ladurée** – many have online ordering. | • Great for upscale events or corporate gifts. | ### Quick Steps to Order 1. **Decide on the occasion** (birthday, wedding, corporate gift, etc.) and the cake size/shape you need. 2. **Choose a style** (classic vanilla, chocolate, vegan, gluten‑free, custom design, etc.). 3. **Pick a vendor** from the table above that matches your location and budget. 4. **Place the order**: - If ordering online, fill out the form, upload any design files, and pay securely. - If calling, have the cake details ready (size, flavor, message, delivery date/time). 5. **Confirm delivery**: double‑check the address, delivery window, and any special instructions. ### Example Order (Local Bakery) - **Bakery**: “Sweet Treats Bakery” (123 Main St, Springfield) - **Cake**: 8‑inch round, chocolate, “Happy Birthday” in gold lettering - **Delivery**: 12‑Oct‑2026, 2 pm–4 pm window - **Contact**: 555‑123‑4567 or order@sweettreats.com Just give them a call or send an email with those details, and they’ll handle the rest! --- If you let me know your city or zip code, I can pull up specific bakeries or delivery services in your area. Happy cake hunting!
